+# Authenticated accepted-predecessor lifecycle qualification
+
+Source: [`d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39`](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/commit/d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39). Branch: [research/incremental-revision-lifecycle-20261022](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/tree/research/incremental-revision-lifecycle-20261022). Exact-source [CI 39679768047](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/runs/39679768047), job 119498882697, completed successfully on 2026-10-22. Evidence provenance is the commit introducing this directory; its exact SHA is recorded in the [canonical Research OS checkpoint](https://app.notion.com/p/3fb3e523d7ab81c68c89c1442eb0bb05) and final delivery.
+
+## Result and scope
+
+**WARRANTED:** the existing MathGraph incremental checker can carry accepted evidence through forty successive controlled changes, including cumulative edits and restorations, while its complete measured lifecycle beats direct fresh Rust verification of the same actual exports. This includes genuine genesis checking, constructor/start, source production, authentication, identity update, actual selected checking, receipt/head persistence and supported shutdown.
+
+The pinned real Lean 4.35.0/Std workloads contain 3,436 and 11,653 obligations. Each of five paired sequences makes ten four-step cycles: early edit; unrelated edit retaining the early edit; early restoration retaining the unrelated edit; unrelated restoration. Each acceptance names its immediate accepted predecessor. These are continuing revisions, rather than forty independent forks from genesis. This extends the prior qualified warm-only result; it does not replace that stronger per-edit warm evidence with lifecycle averages.
+
+## Measured economics
+
+The primary comparison is a separately timed uninterrupted incremental lifecycle against forty-one fresh Rust processes on genesis and the same forty sealed revision exports. Direct input preparation occurs before its timer, favoring direct Rust. Arm order alternates over five pairs. Qualification oracles and evidence packaging occur outside both primary intervals.
+
+| Obligations | Fresh Rust lifecycle median | Incremental lifecycle median | Wall reduction | Rust/incremental |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+|3,436|11.371610s|8.080982s|28.9372%|1.40721x|
+|11,653|54.792482s|33.506680s|38.8480%|1.63527x|
+
+Both profiles win 5/5 pairs. The pointwise paired-bootstrap 95% candidate/direct ratio intervals are [0.599858,0.711717] and [0.545923,0.619720], respectively, using 10,000 resamples. The reported ratio is the ratio of arm medians, not the median of five per-pair ratios. These are repeated same-host observations with warm OS caches, not cross-host or simultaneous confidence guarantees.
+
+Continuous CPU medians are 11.374423→8.078343s (28.9780% reduction) and 54.792057→33.563868s (38.7432%). Separate interleaved API component sums are 11.803732→8.250252s and 53.281320→31.043097s. Component sums and phase medians are not substitutes for the primary uninterrupted wall measurement.
+
+Fresh genesis/start API wall medians within the continuous arms are 3.753791s original and 14.935065s expanded. Forty accepted-update API sums have medians 3.993971s and 17.788029s. These are separately summarized quantities; adding their medians does not reconstruct a lifecycle median. The primary outer timer also includes constructor, close and compact recording.
+
+Warm continuous per-edit API medians, pooled descriptively over 50 observations per edit, are 112.042ms early /75.509ms unrelated original and 499.148ms /472.530ms expanded. Interleaved same-input fresh Rust command medians are 289.584/288.308ms and 1297.726/1279.427ms. These separately observed warm medians are contextual, not a replacement paired speedup qualification.
+
+Separate final forty-step expected-head recovery takes 8.087556s setup and 0.054940s close original; 32.818418s setup and 0.120544s close expanded. Independent snapshot/index checks occur between those components, so their sum is not an uninterrupted cold elapsed measurement. Recovery authenticates prior genesis acceptance and genuinely replays accepted revisions; it does not claim a new full genesis check. There is one recovery observation per profile, with logically cold retained processes and warm OS caches, excluded from primary lifecycle economics. Actual lifecycle observations qualify forty updates; there is no projected crossover claim for other history lengths.
+
+[Phase analysis](phases/actual-ci/analysis.json) uses exact arithmetic on the original published ZIP. Expanded pooled update time is 42.999% persistence, 22.724% complete materialization/hash and 2.127% identity. Corresponding original shares are 23.754%, 26.014% and 2.016%. Promotion is nested within persistence and must not be counted again. Native finish still includes full index cloning/all-component root advancement, so it is not pure affected-cone time. No cause is assigned to residual gaps.
+
+One forty-update original sequence authenticates 4,764 delta bytes while materializing/hashing 636,892,477 complete-export bytes; expanded authenticates 4,795 delta bytes while materializing/hashing 2,564,646,194 bytes. Promotion reads the entire successor again inside persistence. Complete export disk writes are zero for these updates, but sealed memfd writes, hashing, baseline IO and small durable objects still occur. This byte accounting makes the remaining linear work explicit.
+
+Post-phase memory observations are RSS and cumulative VmHWM from the interleaved arm, which also contains oracle/reference state. Missing exited processes are missing measurements. The uninterrupted arms have no continuous aggregate peak-memory measurement; no aggregate peak-memory saving is claimed. Selected checking differs between profiles (early/unrelated 413/1 versus 672/260), so these two workload sizes do not establish constant affected-cone scaling.
+
+## Implementation and trust boundary
+
+`RevisionChainSession` retains the existing producer/exporter, native graph/SCC state and genuine Rust parser after each accepted revision. Versioned chain heads bind the immediate parent head and evidence, revision number, complete bounded source capture, exact delta/export identities and producer policy. Source capture covers all six pinned application files; the actual producer compares the complete local environment. Reported names and patches are assertions, not authority.
+
+The HMAC issuer/key model, verifier policy, conservative applicability predicate, genuine checker and MathGraph resolver remain in use. The new versioned state-continuation implementation is additional trusted code. Acceptance promotes source/export/layout/index/receipt/head only after checking and persistence. Any failure poisons the live processes. A receipt orphaned by later persistence failure is historical evidence, not an accepted successor head. Changed DAG rows still pass through the genuine parser when selected checking is empty.
+
+Cold recovery authenticates all referenced objects and reproduces source/delta history from genesis before reinstating historical authenticated envelopes. The caller must supply an externally retained expected head. HMAC authenticates a historical prefix; it provides no generic latestness or rollback service. Current rejected or UNKNOWN source does not inherit historical current acceptance. Semantic restoration may retain unused appended DAG rows and need not restore the original export SHA.
+
+The source/export/parser/identity executable bridge remains an explicit trust assumption tested by finite differential controls. No whole-pipeline formal proof is claimed. Content hashes identify bytes under their cryptographic assumptions; they do not prove semantic equivalence.
+
+## Correctness and negative controls
+
+- Exact-source CI preserves all 197 original, 335 native, 719 independent replay/full-kernel and 251 original-binary gates, plus 246 original and 229 expanded protected gates. The old 251 economic NO_SPEEDUP remains separate from its passing correctness gates.
+- There are 32 new chain/recovery/adversarial controls per profile, 64 total. They include forged HMACs, changed unauthenticated deltas, altered source captures, wrong parents, environment/version drift, source modifications outside the reported region, false name hints, axiom/kind changes, invalid source proofs, foreign issuers and policy mismatch.
+- Storage controls cover head, source capture, current receipt, transition, delta, representation, genesis, baseline receipt and baseline export corruption; missing latest heads cannot fall back to an older prefix. Persistence failure cannot promote a head. Recovery after refusals and real dependency-edge fallback/restoration are checked against the full-index path and fresh Rust.
+- Two actual kernel-negative exports per profile exercise malformed unused DAG bytes at zero selected obligations and an authenticated invalid definition proof. Retained, fresh Rust, normal C++ and paranoid C++ must reject with an actual rejection exit. Policy refusal/UNKNOWN is distinct from mathematical kernel rejection; no timeout, unsupported input or loader failure counts as rejection.
+- All 400 interleaved accepted revision decisions have exact full-index/fingerprint/partition parity and fresh full Rust agreement; representative states also receive Python-index, C++ and paranoid checks. The separate continuous arms bind every actual export and acceptance to those independent witnesses. The independent stdlib artifact reader passes on the exact original ZIP: 10 paired interleaved lifetimes, 400 accepted revisions, 3,017,800 per-declaration decisions, 2,440 signed-object links and 448 compressed archives. It independently recomputes all 88 economic series and 880,000 bootstrap resamples. Four hundred additional continuous revision receipts are bound to the interleaved full-index/kernel audit. The reader imports no incremental engine, producer controller or project benchmark. It enumerates 16 unique exact inputs, 12 accepted and 4 rejected, for separate kernel replay; its own result explicitly says that it runs no fresh kernel. Both exact 32-control matrices pass. The declaration-own-hash/export bridge remains the frozen full-native/Python witness, rather than an independently proved parser bridge.
+- All five actual-artifact falsifiers refuse in memory: fake zero-work success, missing complete input, changed compressed-input identity, raw parent substitution and omitted changed-input coverage. The frozen reader files and qualified source remain unchanged throughout; there are no actual-artifact reader repairs. See [independent assessment](independent-review/actual-ci/assessment.json) and [falsifiers](independent-review/actual-ci/falsifiers.json). Compact topology controls omit the prior step2 receipt: that first parent is checked by identifier and all decision origins; subsequent links are exact. The main 400-step audit is separate and complete.
+- Separate [fresh replay](fresh-kernels/summary.json) executes 48 real Rust/C++/paranoid processes over 16 (12 accepted and 4 rejected) exact published inputs; all three oracles accept every one of the 12 accepted inputs and reject every one of the 4 invalid inputs with exact exit codes 0/1. There are no timeouts, unsupported verdicts or checker failures. Input bytes and executed binaries remain unchanged before/after checking. This replay invokes independently fresh full Rust, pinned normal C++ and pinned paranoid C++ without importing the incremental engine or cache authority. Rust is locally built from exact qualified source; historical CI Rust executable-byte equality is not assumed. Historical secret HMACs are observed through issuer-audit witnesses, not publicly reauthenticated without the private CI key.
+
+## Artifacts and replay
+
+Compact [artifact 12390854795](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/runs/39679768047/artifacts/12390854795): 1,250,298,163 bytes, provider SHA256 `878fbeeb4f6241084fd89ca20a2b9b8077c9071e2ada7e2e0b94d054e743d766`. The reconstructed local original ZIP has the exact provider size and SHA256; all 9,482 member CRCs pass. Eleven ordered lossless XZ parts are listed in [packaging/manifest.json](packaging/manifest.json), each at most 48 MiB. Their concatenation is 528,312,196 bytes, SHA256 `a78f2817c3f6f8c1eca9c50dc851baa2a9f5bf9d92329378114a2cca2df9fd13`. Separate root reconstruction from the copied preservation parts verifies every part, writes and rehashes the original ZIP, and checks every member CRC; see [root preservation proof](packaging/root-reconstruction-proof.json). This packaging is storage/transport only; compression is not runtime performance evidence.
+
+Full [artifact 12391188911](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/runs/39679768047/artifacts/12391188911): 4,486,141,109 bytes, provider SHA256 `dbb4e7819ddfe1c07f4dd4fbeb98fa2005d6cfaab8b66d8b8dfe4ea54a1714d7`. It was not downloaded or independently byte-hashed here. Keep provider metadata distinct from locally verified compact bytes.
+
+Transport issue: this workspace's proxy refused the native blob redirect and the GitHub connector rejected the compact archive above its 512 MiB limit. A separate transport-only CI run [CI 39698586368](https://github.com/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/runs/39698586368), source `3ec0191126fa0f544fadec05435c02ac2be0c8aa`, split the exact published ZIP, without rerunning qualification or changing its source. Reconstructed compact bytes must match the original provider digest. Preserve the transport manifest, part digests and run metadata.
+
+The executable [replay-evidence.sh](replay-evidence.sh) performs reconstruction, exact-source review, directed falsifiers, all fresh kernels and phase arithmetic. Supply a fresh absolute output directory and the three pinned/exact-source checker paths. It creates a detached runtime worktree. Reconstruction writes a 1.25 GB ZIP; the full audit decodes a 344 MB summary. Historical local reviewer unit tests retain their original smoke-fixture paths; those development logs are lineage, while the actual-artifact replay uses only the committed archive and source.
+
+Replay manually from a clone containing the evidence and exact source:
+
+1. Verify `SHA256SUMS`, then reconstruct the exact compact ZIP from ordered parts. Choose an existing output parent directory and a fresh output file:
+
+   ```sh
+   python3 packaging/reconstruct_archive.py --manifest packaging/manifest.json \
+     --output /fresh/output/ci-compact.zip
+   ```
+
+   The helper verifies all part sizes/digests, concatenated XZ size/digest, original ZIP size/digest, written output bytes and every ZIP member CRC. See [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md).
+2. Create a detached worktree at `d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39`; do not run source-bound replay from the later evidence commit.
+3. Run the preserved independent stdlib reader on the archive with expected source and observed CI provenance. It must reconstruct receipt/parent linkage, reuse partitions and raw input coverage without importing the incremental controller, then recompute economics and run its falsifiers.
+
+   ```sh
+   python3 independent-review/reviewer.py --artifact /absolute/path/to/ci-compact.zip \
+     --repo /absolute/path/to/detached-runtime-source \
+     --source d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39 --output /fresh/output/review/ci-review.json
+   python3 independent-review/run_falsifiers.py --artifact /absolute/path/to/ci-compact.zip \
+     --repo /absolute/path/to/detached-runtime-source \
+     --source d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39 --output /fresh/output/review/falsifiers.json
+   ```
+4. Run the preserved `fresh_kernel_replay.py` using the reader's newly generated `inputs.json`, exact Rust build and pinned normal/paranoid C++ kernels. It must check every actual input digest before and after all three genuine kernel processes.
+
+   ```sh
+   python3 independent-review/fresh_kernel_replay.py --artifact /absolute/path/to/ci-compact.zip \
+     --inputs /fresh/output/review/inputs.json --repo /absolute/path/to/detached-runtime-source \
+     --source d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39 \
+     --rust /absolute/path/to/exact-runtime/release/sokonanoda \
+     --cpp /absolute/path/to/lean-4.35.0/bin/leanchecker \
+     --paranoid /absolute/path/to/lean-4.35.0/bin/leanchecker-paranoid --out /fresh/output/kernels
+   ```
+
+   Build Rust with `cargo +1.95.0 build --release --locked --bin sokonanoda` in the detached runtime source. Use the pinned toolchain/binary setup in that source's `experiments/incremental/setup.sh`; the replay script checks normal/paranoid executable SHA256 against exact `pins.json`. The replay output directory must not already exist.
+5. For a new full qualification, use the exact-source workflow/setup commands. A fresh run creates its own private HMAC authority; the historical issuer key is not published.
+
+Preserve source/binary hashes, raw paired measurements, independent reader source/tests/RED repairs/falsifiers, fresh-kernel configs/logs/input hashes, phase analysis, metadata and ROS readback proof. Do not silently replace actual historical failures with later summaries.
+
+## Remaining residual
+
+Per-update complete export materialization/hash, full successor readback, full index cloning and remaining declaration/receipt scans still scale with total development size. Cold recovery scales with accepted history. **UNKNOWN:** how to remove those full-development costs while preserving the same authenticated source-to-export integrity and independently checkable acceptance boundary. The qualified lifecycle speedup is bounded and concrete; total verification is not yet asymptotically proportional only to the affected dependency cone.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reconstruct exact qualification ZIP from authenticated transport envelopes."""
+import hashlib,json,zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+metadata=json.loads((root.parent/'artifact-transport/artifacts-now.json').read_text())
+artifacts=metadata['artifacts']
+proof={'schema':'mathgraph.exact-artifact-reconstruction.v1','parts':[]}
+with zipfile.ZipFile(root/'transport-partmanifest.zip') as z:
+    assert z.testzip() is None
+    for n in z.namelist():
+        assert n in ('transport-manifest.json','original-artifact.json','original-run.json')
+        (root/n).write_bytes(z.read(n))
+manifest=json.loads((root/'transport-manifest.json').read_text())
+assert manifest['qualified_source']=='d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39'
+assert manifest['qualification_run']==39679768047
+expected=manifest['original_archive_sha256']
+assert expected=='878fbeeb4f6241084fd89ca20a2b9b8077c9071e2ada7e2e0b94d054e743d766'
+out=root/'revision-chain-summaries-d1b2244.zip.part'
+total=0;whole=hashlib.sha256()
+with out.open('xb') as dest:
+    for i,entry in enumerate(manifest['parts']):
+        p=root/('transport-part%02d.zip'%i)
+        outer=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+        a=next(a for a in artifacts if a['name']=='revision-chain-transport-part%02d-d1b2244'%i)
+        assert p.stat().st_size==a['size_in_bytes'] and a['digest']=='sha256:'+outer
+        digest=hashlib.sha256();size=0
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(p) as z:
+            assert z.namelist()==[entry['name']]
+            with z.open(entry['name']) as source:
+                while True:
+                    b=source.read(4*1024*1024)
+                    if not b:break
+                    dest.write(b);size+=len(b);total+=len(b);digest.update(b);whole.update(b)
+        assert size==entry['bytes'] and digest.hexdigest()==entry['sha256']
+        proof['parts'].append(dict(part=i,artifact_id=a['id'],outer_bytes=p.stat().st_size,
+                                   outer_sha256=outer,inner=entry))
+assert total==manifest['original_archive_bytes']==1250298163
+assert whole.hexdigest()==expected
+with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as z:
+    assert z.testzip() is None
+    proof['zip_members']=len(z.infolist())
+out.rename(out.with_suffix(''))
+proof.update(passed=True,original_bytes=total,original_sha256=expected,
+             qualified_source=manifest['qualified_source'],qualification_run=39679768047,
+             original_artifact_id=12390854795,zip_crc_passed=True)
+(root/'reconstruction-proof.json').write_text(json.dumps(proof,indent=2)+'\n')
+print(json.dumps(proof,indent=2))

+name: Qualified revision evidence byte transport
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  actions: read
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+jobs:

+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    steps:
+      - name: Download and authenticate the exact qualified archive
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir parts
+          gh api /repos/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/artifacts/12390854795 > original-artifact.json
+          gh api /repos/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/runs/39679768047 > original-run.json
+          gh api /repos/metalogiclabs/mathgraph-lean-kernel/actions/artifacts/12390854795/zip > qualified-evidence.zip
+          python3 - <<'PYTHON'
+          import hashlib,json,pathlib,zipfile
+          source='d1b22447d23a928ae536cbe838a47fc9682a4b39'
+          expected='878fbeeb4f6241084fd89ca20a2b9b8077c9071e2ada7e2e0b94d054e743d766'
+          archive=pathlib.Path('qualified-evidence.zip')
+          metadata=json.loads(pathlib.Path('original-artifact.json').read_text())
+          run=json.loads(pathlib.Path('original-run.json').read_text())
+          assert run['id']==39679768047 and run['head_sha']==source
+          assert run['status']=='completed' and run['conclusion']=='success'
+          assert metadata['id']==12390854795 and metadata['workflow_run']['head_sha']==source
+          assert metadata['workflow_run']['id']==39679768047
+          assert metadata['size_in_bytes']==1250298163
+          assert metadata['digest']=='sha256:'+expected
+          assert archive.stat().st_size==1250298163
+          digest=hashlib.file_digest(archive.open('rb'),'sha256').hexdigest()
+          assert digest==expected
+          with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as z:
+              assert z.testzip() is None
+          pieces=[]
+          with archive.open('rb') as f:
+              for index in range(4):

+              assert f.read(1)==b''

+
+The ZIP is streamed; there is no extraction. Members are mapped from historical
+CI paths to ZIP-root-relative names. Before/after source pins are compared with
+git show of the explicitly supplied commit. Full review requires both 5x40
+profiles, alternating uninterrupted 40/41 candidate/direct histories, 40-step
+cold replay, complete actual-input coverage, both exact 32-control matrices and
+their complete rejected inputs. The local smoke's reported older dirty HEAD is
+retained in the output; only its exact code-byte match to the supplied commit is
+verified. Missing local CI/control scope is explicitly reported UNQUALIFIED.
+Lifecycle summary JSON and the manifest descriptors for exactly the four
+frozen chain-test/control report families allow up to 512 MiB. Decoded control
+summaries share that scoped bound. Generic logs, indexes, result witnesses and
+continuous summaries retain 64 MiB limits; complete exports are streamed.

+Outputs:
+  --output JSON: independent findings, source/reader hashes and bounded scopes.
+  inputs.json beside --output: unique accepted/rejected complete inputs, with
+    sha256, bytes, expected_returncode, member, encoding, profile, roles,
+    observations and compressed member SHA/size. Accepted observations also
+    include selected indices and result/evidence references for optional fresh
+    full-parser selected checking. Failed review clears this manifest to [].

+  origin, and all arithmetic/bootstrap statistics. Declaration own and complex

+  Historical HMAC validity is NOT reauthenticated without the private CI key;
+  only exact object addresses, domains and source/policy/predecessor linkage are
+  independently checked. Prior CI publisher completion is observed, not used
+  as a substitute for these lifecycle checks. No fresh kernel is run here.

+"""Strict streaming artifact access. Standard library only; never extracts a ZIP."""
+import contextlib
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+import stat
+import zipfile
+
+JSON_LOG_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+LIFECYCLE_SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+def require(value, message):
+    if not value:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def hexid(value):
+    return type(value) is str and len(value) == 64 and all(c in '0123456789abcdef' for c in value)
+
+
+def strict_object(pairs):
+    result = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        require(key not in result, 'duplicate JSON key: ' + key)
+        result[key] = value
+    return result
+
+
+def loads(raw):
+    return json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=strict_object,
+                      parse_constant=lambda value: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError('nonfinite JSON: ' + value)))
+
+
+def canonical(value):
+    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False).encode()
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value)).hexdigest()
+
+
+class Artifacts:
+    def __init__(self, path):
+        self.path = Path(path).resolve()
+        self.zip = None
+        self.opened_signatures = {}
+        self.zip_signature = self.signature(self.path) if self.path.is_file() else None
+        if self.path.is_file():
+            self.zip = zipfile.ZipFile(self.path)
+            self.members = {}
+            for info in self.zip.infolist():
+                name = self.safe(info.filename.rstrip('/'))
+                if info.is_dir():
+                    continue
+                require(name not in self.members, 'duplicate ZIP member: ' + name)
+                require(not stat.S_ISLNK(info.external_attr >> 16), 'ZIP symlink refused')
+                self.members[name] = info
+        else:
+            require(self.path.is_dir(), 'artifact directory/ZIP is missing')
+            self.members = {str(p.relative_to(self.path)): p for p in self.path.rglob('*') if p.is_file()}
+        candidates = [name for name in self.members if name == 'summary.json' or name.endswith('/revision-chain/summary.json') or name == 'revision-chain/summary.json']
+        candidates = [name for name in candidates if loads(self.read(name, LIFECYCLE_SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES)).get('schema') == 'mathgraph.authenticated-revision-chain-lifecycle.v1']
+        require(len(candidates) == 1, 'exactly one lifecycle summary is required')
+        self.summary_member = candidates[0]
+        self.lifecycle = str(PurePosixPath(self.summary_member).parent)
+        if self.lifecycle == '.':
+            self.lifecycle = ''
+        self.artifact = self.lifecycle[:-len('revision-chain')].rstrip('/') if self.lifecycle.endswith('revision-chain') else ''
+        report = self.json(self.summary_member)
+        blobs = [p['genesis']['baseline_witness'] for pr in report.get('profiles', {}).values() for p in pr.get('pairs', [])]
+        require(blobs, 'summary has no actual input witness')
+        first = blobs[0]
+        rel = first['artifact_relative_path']
+        require(first['path'].endswith(rel), 'original archive path does not end in artifact-relative path')
+        self.original = first['path'][:-len(rel)].rstrip('/')
+        self.descriptors = {}
+        self.archive_checks = 0
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def signature(path):
+        st = path.stat()
+        return st.st_dev, st.st_ino, st.st_size, st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_ctime_ns
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def safe(name):
+        require(type(name) is str and '\\' not in name and name and not name.startswith('/'), 'unsafe artifact member')
+        parts = PurePosixPath(name).parts
+        require('..' not in parts and '.' not in parts, 'artifact traversal refused')
+        return '/'.join(parts)
+
+    def join(self, *parts):
+        return self.safe('/'.join(str(p).strip('/') for p in parts if str(p).strip('/')))
+
+    def map(self, recorded):
+        require(type(recorded) is str, 'recorded path must be text')
+        if recorded.startswith(self.original + '/'):
+            return self.join(self.lifecycle, recorded[len(self.original) + 1:])
+        if recorded.startswith('artifacts/'):
+            return self.join(self.artifact, recorded[len('artifacts/'):])
+        if '/artifacts/' in recorded:
+            return self.join(self.artifact, recorded.split('/artifacts/', 1)[1])
+        if not recorded.startswith('/'):
+            direct = self.safe(recorded)
+            if direct in self.members:
+                return direct
+        raise ValueError('recorded path is outside artifact: ' + recorded)
+
+    @contextlib.contextmanager
+    def open(self, name):
+        name = self.safe(name)
+        require(name in self.members, 'missing artifact object: ' + name)
+        if self.zip:
+            require(self.signature(self.path) == self.zip_signature, 'artifact ZIP changed during review')
+            with self.zip.open(self.members[name]) as stream:
+                yield stream
+        else:
+            path = self.members[name]
+            require(path.resolve().is_relative_to(self.path), 'artifact symlink escapes root')
+            signature = self.signature(path)
+            if name in self.opened_signatures:
+                require(self.opened_signatures[name] == signature, 'artifact file changed during review: ' + name)
+            self.opened_signatures[name] = signature
+            with path.open('rb') as stream:
+                yield stream
+
+    def read(self, name, limit=JSON_LOG_MAX_BYTES):
+        with self.open(name) as stream:
+            raw = stream.read(limit + 1)
+        require(len(raw) <= limit, 'JSON/log artifact exceeds reader bound')
+        return raw
+
+    def json(self, name):
+        limit = LIFECYCLE_SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES if name == getattr(self, 'summary_member', None) else JSON_LOG_MAX_BYTES
+        return loads(self.read(name, limit))
+
+    def stream_hash(self, name, gzip_encoded=False):
+        h, length = hashlib.sha256(), 0
+        with self.open(name) as raw:
+            with (gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=raw) if gzip_encoded else contextlib.nullcontext(raw)) as stream:
+                for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1 << 20), b''):
+                    h.update(chunk)
+                    length += len(chunk)
+                    require(length <= 1024 * 1024 * 1024, 'single artifact exceeds 1GiB review bound')
+        return h.hexdigest(), length
+
+    def archive(self, record):
+        for key in ('sha256', 'uncompressed_sha256'):
+            require(hexid(record.get(key)), 'invalid archive digest')
+        for key in ('bytes', 'uncompressed_bytes'):
+            require(type(record.get(key)) is int and record[key] >= 0, 'invalid archive byte count')
+        require(record.get('encoding', 'gzip') == 'gzip', 'unsupported archive encoding')
+        member = self.join(self.lifecycle, record['artifact_relative_path'])
+        metadata = tuple(record[k] for k in ('sha256', 'bytes', 'uncompressed_sha256', 'uncompressed_bytes'))
+        if member in self.descriptors:
+            require(self.descriptors[member] == metadata, 'contradictory cached archive descriptor')
+            # The directory development mode is mutable. Recheck its cached
+            # file signature; ZIP mode is bound to the unchanged ZIP identity.
+            with self.open(member):
+                pass
+        else:
+            require(self.stream_hash(member) == metadata[:2], 'compressed archive SHA/size mismatch: ' + member)
+            require(self.stream_hash(member, True) == metadata[2:], 'uncompressed archive SHA/size mismatch: ' + member)
+            self.descriptors[member] = metadata
+            self.archive_checks += 1
+        return member
+
+    def archive_json(self, record):
+        member = self.archive(record)
+        with self.open(member) as raw, gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=raw) as stream:
+            value = stream.read(64 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)
+        require(len(value) <= 64 * 1024 * 1024, 'compressed JSON exceeds reader bound')
+        return loads(value)
+
+    def saved(self, recorded):
+        member = self.map(recorded)
+        return self.saved_member(member)
+
+    def saved_member(self, member):
+        if member in self.members:
+            return self.read(member)
+        record = self.json(member + '.archive.json')
+        archive = self.archive(record)
+        with self.open(archive) as raw, gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=raw) as stream:
+            value = stream.read(64 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)
+        require(len(value) <= 64 * 1024 * 1024, 'saved JSON/log exceeds reader bound')
+        return value
+
+    def descriptors_in(self, value):
+        if type(value) is dict:
+            if {'artifact_relative_path', 'uncompressed_sha256', 'uncompressed_bytes', 'sha256', 'bytes'} <= set(value):
+                self.archive(value)
+            for child in value.values():
+                self.descriptors_in(child)
+        elif type(value) is list:
+            for child in value:
+                self.descriptors_in(child)
+
+    def assert_stable(self):
+        if self.zip:
+            require(self.signature(self.path) == self.zip_signature, 'artifact ZIP changed during review')
+        else:
+            for name, signature in self.opened_signatures.items():
+                require(name in self.members and self.signature(self.members[name]) == signature,
+                        'artifact file changed during review: ' + name)

+"""Independent review of the frozen 32-control matrix. Standard library only.
+
+Historical private-key HMAC validity is not reauthenticated here. The compact
+artifact preserves full-native index outputs and genuine process outcome/output
+witnesses for topology controls, plus exact complete rejected inputs. It omits
+the restored step-2 acceptance record; the first topology parent's identifier is
+checked against its decision origins and later topology links are exact.
+"""
+import ast
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+from artifacts import canonical, hexid, loads, require
+from reuse_rule import validate_index, validate_partition
+
+CONTROL_SOURCE = 'experiments/incremental/test_revision_chain_controls.py'
+# The exact four frozen control/chain summary wrappers retain complete
+# per-declaration decisions. Keep their metadata cap separate from generic logs.
+CONTROL_REPORT_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024
+NEGATIVES = ('signed-invalid-definition-proof', 'unused-malformed-dag-zero-selected')
+PARTITION_FIELDS = frozenset(('actual_kernel_checked','actual_kernel_total','independently_replayed_reused',
+                              'checked_indices','reused_indices','identity_witnesses_checked'))
+
+
+def required_names(repo, source):
+    require(re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}',source) is not None, 'exact source SHA required for controls')
+    raw=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(repo),'show',source+':'+CONTROL_SOURCE])
+    tree=ast.parse(raw)
+    values=[node.value for node in tree.body if isinstance(node,ast.Assign) and
+            any(isinstance(target,ast.Name) and target.id=='REQUIRED_CONTROLS' for target in node.targets)]
+    require(len(values)==1, 'frozen source has ambiguous required control matrix')
+    names=ast.literal_eval(values[0])
+    require(type(names) is tuple and len(names)==32 and len(set(names))==32 and
+            all(type(name) is str and name for name in names), 'frozen required matrix is not exactly32')
+    return names
+
+
+def validate_header(report, expected, source, profile):
+    require(type(report) is dict and report.get('schema')=='mathgraph.revision-chain-controls.v1' and
+            report.get('source_sha')==source and report.get('passed') is True,
+            'controls report incomplete, wrong-source or wrong-domain')
+    require(report.get('profile')==('original-v1' if profile=='original' else 'std-hashmap-expanded-v1'),
+            'controls workload profile differs')
+    required,rows=report.get('required_controls'),report.get('controls')
+    require(type(required) is list and len(required)==32 and len(set(required))==32 and set(required)==set(expected),
+            'report self-declared required matrix differs from exact frozen32')
+    require(type(rows) is list and len(rows)==32 and
+            all(type(row) is dict and row.get('passed') is True and type(row.get('name')) is str for row in rows),
+            'controls matrix missing/failed actual observations')
+    require(len({row['name'] for row in rows})==32 and {row['name'] for row in rows}==set(expected),
+            'actual controls omitted, duplicated or substituted')
+    return {row['name']:row for row in rows}
+
+
+def validate_result_profile(result,profile,count):
+    require(type(count) is int and count>0 and result.get('producer_provenance',{}).get('profile')==
+            ('original-v1' if profile=='original' else 'std-hashmap-expanded-v1') and
+            type(result.get('counts',{}).get('total')) is int and result['counts']['total']==count,
+            'control result workload profile/count differs from complete baseline reference')
+
+
+def validate_zero_selected_rejection(result,parent_index,parent_evidence):
+    require(hexid(parent_evidence) and result.get('previous_evidence')==parent_evidence,
+            'zero-selected rejection targets a foreign admitted parent')
+    counts=result.get('counts',{})
+    require(all(type(counts.get(k)) is int and counts[k]==v for k,v in
+            dict(total=parent_index['count'],scheduled=0,reused=parent_index['count'],invalidated=0).items()) and
+            counts.get('rechecked') is None, 'zero-selected rejection hid scheduled or completed obligations')
+    decisions=result.get('decisions')
+    require(type(decisions) is list and len(decisions)==parent_index['count'],
+            'zero-selected rejection omitted complete reused decisions')
+    for decision,row in zip(decisions,parent_index['declarations']):
+        require(type(decision.get('index')) is int and decision['index']==row['index'] and
+                decision.get('name')==row['name'] and decision.get('status')=='VERIFIED_REUSED' and
+                decision.get('evidence_id')==parent_evidence and
+                canonical(decision.get('dependency_witness'))==canonical(dict(own=row['own'],closure=row['closure'],direct=row['deps'])),
+                'zero-selected rejection changed a parent decision witness or evidence origin')
+
+
+def _configuration(value):
+    require(type(value) is dict and set(value)=={'export_file_path','use_stdin','permitted_axioms',
+            'unpermitted_axiom_hard_error','num_threads','nat_extension','string_extension','print_success_message'} and
+            type(value['export_file_path']) is str and value['use_stdin'] is False and
+            value['permitted_axioms']==['propext','Classical.choice','Quot.sound'] and
+            value['unpermitted_axiom_hard_error'] is True and type(value['num_threads']) is int and
+            value['num_threads']==1 and value['nat_extension'] is True and value['string_extension'] is True and
+            value['print_success_message'] is True, 'control full-kernel/index configuration differs from policy')
+    return value
+
+
+def _outputs(store, process, code):
+    require(type(process) is dict and type(process.get('returncode')) is int and
+            process['returncode']==code and process.get('timed_out') is False,
+            'control real process failed, timed out or has wrong rejection code')
+    require(type(process.get('command')) is list and process['command'] and
+            all(type(part) is str for part in process['command']), 'control process command missing')
+    for kind in ('stdout','stderr'):
+        raw=store.saved(process[kind+'_path'])
+        require(hexid(process.get(kind+'_sha256')) and hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()==process[kind+'_sha256'],
+                'actual control process output changed: '+kind)
+
+
+def _native_index(store, folder, expected_binary):
+    value=loads(store.saved_member(store.join(folder,'index.json')))
+    process=loads(store.saved_member(store.join(folder,'process.json')))
+    _outputs(store,process,0)
+    require(len(process['command'])==2 and process['command'][0]==expected_binary,
+            'topology full-native process uses a different executable')
+    stdout=loads(store.saved(process['stdout_path']))
+    require(canonical(stdout)==canonical(value), 'topology full index differs from actual native stdout')
+    validate_index(value)
+    config=_configuration(loads(store.saved(process['command'][1])))
+    return value,config
+
+
+def _manifest(store):
+    member=store.join(store.artifact,'revision-control-archive.json')
+    require(member in store.members, 'missing control summary compressed-byte manifest')
+    records=store.json(member)
+    expected={store.join(store.artifact,folder,'summary.json.gz') for folder in
+              ('revision-chain-tests-original','revision-chain-tests-expanded',
+               'revision-chain-controls-original','revision-chain-controls-expanded')}
+    require(type(records) is list and len(records)==4, 'compressed control/archive manifest must cover all four reports')
+    indexed={}
+    for record in records:
+        require(type(record) is dict and set(record)=={'path','sha256','bytes','uncompressed_path',
+                'uncompressed_sha256','uncompressed_bytes'} and
+                hexid(record['sha256']) and hexid(record['uncompressed_sha256']) and
+                type(record['bytes']) is int and record['bytes']>0 and
+                type(record['uncompressed_bytes']) is int and record['uncompressed_bytes']>0,
+                'invalid compressed control report descriptor')
+        path=store.map(record['path'])
+        require(path not in indexed and path in expected and
+                store.map(record['uncompressed_path'])==path[:-3], 'substituted or duplicate compressed control report')

+"""Independent standard-library checks of lifecycle arithmetic and statistics.
+
+No production adapter, benchmark, verifier, or issuer code is imported. These
+checks establish consistency of the recorded observations, not elapsed-time
+authenticity or kernel acceptance. Historical issuer HMACs are outside scope.
+"""
+import json
+import math
+import random
+import statistics
+
+
+PRIMARY = 'Sum of measured constructor/start, all accepted apply APIs, supported shutdown. No projected amortization.'
+DIRECT = 'Sum of actual fresh full Rust command wall durations at genesis and every exact sealed revision; process creation and exit included.'
+CONTINUOUS = 'Uninterrupted constructor/start through all accepted applies and supported close; no intervening independent oracles or evidence packaging.'
+CONTINUOUS_DIRECT = 'Uninterrupted fresh full Rust commands at genesis and every identical accepted revision; exact input preparation is outside timing.'
+COMPONENT_SCOPE = ('Observed constructor/start + every production apply + supported close API intervals; '
+                   'intervening independent oracles and harness evidence packaging are excluded. '
+                   'Direct comparator is a fresh full Rust command at genesis and every exact accepted revision.')
+CPU_SCOPE = ('Adapter + completed-child resource CPU + live producer/index/kernel procfs CPU; '
+             'SC_CLK_TCK granularity applies to live daemons. Separately summed observed API intervals; '
+             'direct full Rust uses completed-child CPU per actual fresh command.')
+CLOSE_SCOPE = 'Supported adapter close terminates/waits daemons and removes private files; no Rust EOF/destructor guarantee.'
+WARM_SCOPE = 'warm authenticated session update versus fresh full Rust command'
+
+
+def require(value, message):
+    if not value:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def canonical(value):
+    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True,
+                      allow_nan=False).encode()
+
+
+def same(actual, expected, label):
+    require(canonical(actual) == canonical(expected), label + ' changed')
+
+
+def duration(value, label, *, positive=False):
+    require(type(value) in (int, float) and math.isfinite(value) and
+            (value > 0 if positive else value >= 0), 'invalid ' + label)
+    return value
+
+
+def integer(value, label, *, minimum=0):
+    require(type(value) is int and value >= minimum, 'invalid ' + label)
+    return value
+
+
+def paired_statistics(candidate, direct, *, seed, bootstrap_repetitions=10000):
+    """Paired resampling of median ratios, independently recomputed in full."""
+    require(type(candidate) is list and type(direct) is list and
+            len(candidate) == len(direct) and len(candidate) > 0, 'missing paired durations')
+    for label, observations in (('candidate', candidate), ('direct', direct)):
+        for value in observations:
+            duration(value, label + ' observation', positive=True)
+    integer(seed, 'bootstrap seed')
+    integer(bootstrap_repetitions, 'bootstrap count', minimum=1)
+    count = len(candidate)
+    ratio = statistics.median(candidate) / statistics.median(direct)
+    generator = random.Random(seed)
+    resampled_ratios = []
+    for _ in range(bootstrap_repetitions):
+        indices = [generator.randrange(count) for _ in range(count)]
+        candidate_median = statistics.median(candidate[i] for i in indices)
+        direct_median = statistics.median(direct[i] for i in indices)
+        resampled_ratios.append(candidate_median / direct_median)
+    resampled_ratios.sort()
+    interval = [resampled_ratios[int(quantile * (bootstrap_repetitions - 1))]
+                for quantile in (0.025, 0.975)]
+    wins = sum(left < right for left, right in zip(candidate, direct))
+    speedup = ratio < 1 and wins > count / 2 and interval[1] < 1
+    return dict(passed=speedup, status='SPEEDUP' if speedup else 'NO_SPEEDUP',
+                apply_median_wall_seconds=statistics.median(candidate),
+                direct_median_wall_seconds=statistics.median(direct), median_ratio=ratio,
+                paired_wins=wins, paired_count=count,
+                bootstrap_ratio_interval_95=interval,
+                bootstrap_repetitions=bootstrap_repetitions, bootstrap_seed=seed,
+                setup_in_timed_update=False, scope=WARM_SCOPE)
+
+
+def incomplete(expected, count):
+    if count < 5:
+        expected.update(observed_status=expected['status'],
+                        status='INCOMPLETE_FEWER_THAN_FIVE_PAIRS', passed=False)
+    return expected
+
+
+def economic_series(candidate, direct, seed, extras=None):
+    expected = paired_statistics(candidate, direct, seed=seed)
+    expected.update(extras or {})
+    return incomplete(expected, len(candidate))
+
+
+def _seconds_mapping(mapping, label):
+    require(type(mapping) is dict, label + ' is missing')

+
+

+                direct = step['direct_rust']
+                wall_directs.append(duration(direct['wall_seconds'], label + ' direct wall', positive=True))
+                cpu_directs.append(duration(direct['completed_child_cpu_seconds'], label + ' direct CPU'))
+                _seconds_mapping(step['phases'], label + ' phases')
+                require(step['apply_wall_seconds'] >= step['phases']['end_to_end_seconds'],
+                        label + ' apply outer interval excludes production API')

+            close_wall = duration(components['close_wall_seconds'], label + ' close wall')
+            expected = dict(setup_wall_seconds=setup['wall_seconds'], apply_wall_seconds=wall_applies,
+                            close_wall_seconds=close_wall,
+                            direct_genesis_wall_seconds=genesis['wall_seconds'],
+                            direct_revision_wall_seconds=wall_directs, accepted_revisions=revisions,
+                            api_component_sum_wall_seconds=setup['wall_seconds'] + sum(wall_applies) + close_wall,
+                            direct_full_rust_component_sum_wall_seconds=genesis['wall_seconds'] + sum(wall_directs),
+                            scope=COMPONENT_SCOPE, close_scope=CLOSE_SCOPE)
+            same(components, expected, label + ' wall components')
+            cpu_components = pair['cpu_components']
+            close_cpu = duration(cpu_components['close_cpu_seconds'], label + ' close CPU')
+            expected_cpu = dict(setup_cpu_seconds=setup['cpu_seconds'], apply_cpu_seconds=cpu_applies,
+                                close_cpu_seconds=close_cpu,
+                                direct_genesis_cpu_seconds=genesis['completed_child_cpu_seconds'],
+                                direct_revision_cpu_seconds=cpu_directs,
+                                api_component_sum_cpu_seconds=setup['cpu_seconds'] + sum(cpu_applies) + close_cpu,
+                                direct_full_rust_component_sum_cpu_seconds=genesis['completed_child_cpu_seconds'] + sum(cpu_directs),
+                                scope=CPU_SCOPE)
+            same(cpu_components, expected_cpu, label + ' CPU components')
+            elapsed = duration(pair['observed_constructor_through_close_wall_seconds'], label + ' observed elapsed', positive=True)
+            require(elapsed >= expected['api_component_sum_wall_seconds'] + expected['direct_full_rust_component_sum_wall_seconds'],
+                    label + ' observed elapsed excludes measured interleaving')
+            if pair_number == 0:
+                cold = pair['cold_replay']
+                duration(cold['setup_wall_seconds'], label + ' cold setup', positive=True)
+                duration(cold['close_wall_seconds'], label + ' cold close')
+                _seconds_mapping(cold['ready'], label + ' cold ready')
+                require(cold['setup_wall_seconds'] >= cold['ready']['wall_seconds'],
+                        label + ' cold setup excludes replay API')
+            continuous = pair['continuous']
+            same(continuous['order'], ['candidate', 'direct'] if pair_number % 2 == 0 else ['direct', 'candidate'],
+                 label + ' continuous order')
+            require(continuous['completed'] is True, label + ' incomplete continuous pair')
+            candidate, direct = continuous['candidate'], continuous['direct']
+            for name, arm in (('candidate', candidate), ('direct', direct)):
+                require(arm['completed'] is True, label + ' continuous ' + name + ' incomplete')
+                duration(arm['wall_seconds'], label + ' continuous ' + name + ' wall', positive=True)
+                duration(arm['cpu_seconds'], label + ' continuous ' + name + ' CPU', positive=True)
+            require(len(candidate['steps']) == revisions and len(direct['commands']) == revisions + 1,
+                    label + ' continuous revision/command count')
+            command_walls, command_cpus = [], []
+            for revision, command in enumerate(direct['commands']):
+                same(command['revision'], revision, label + ' continuous direct revision')

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Fresh independent kernels on exact published exports; no cache/issuer imports."""
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+import resource
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import time
+import zipfile
+
+
+def sha(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def require(condition, reason):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(reason)
+
+
+def classify(code, timed_out):
+    return ('TIMEOUT' if timed_out else 'ACCEPTED' if code == 0 else
+            'REJECTED' if code == 1 else 'UNSUPPORTED' if code == 2 else
+            'SIGNAL' if code is not None and code < 0 else 'CHECKER_FAILURE')
+
+
+def main():
+    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    for name in ('artifact','inputs','repo','rust','cpp','paranoid','out'):
+        p.add_argument('--'+name,type=Path,required=True)
+    p.add_argument('--source',required=True)
+    p.add_argument('--timeout',type=int,default=300)
+    args=p.parse_args()
+    args.out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=False)
+    report=dict(schema='mathgraph.revision-chain-independent-fresh-kernels.v1',
+                source_sha=args.source,completed=False,passed=False,inputs=[],
+                historical_hmac_reauthenticated=False,
+                host=list(platform.uname()),
+                scope='Fresh full Rust and pinned normal/paranoid C++ on exact artifact export bytes; no incremental engine or cache authority.')
+    def save():
+        (args.out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')
+    save()
+    repo=args.repo.resolve()
+    pins=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',args.source+':experiments/incremental/pins.json'],cwd=repo))
+    binaries={k:getattr(args,k).resolve() for k in ('rust','cpp','paranoid')}
+    binary_hashes={k:sha(v.read_bytes()) for k,v in binaries.items()}
+    require(binary_hashes['cpp']==pins['lean_release_binaries_sha256']['leanchecker'],'normal C++ pin mismatch')
+    require(binary_hashes['paranoid']==pins['lean_release_binaries_sha256']['leanchecker-paranoid'],'paranoid C++ pin mismatch')
+    report['binary_sha256']=binary_hashes
+    report['rust_source_scope']='Locally built exact research source; historical CI binary equality is not assumed.'
+    require(subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=repo,text=True).strip()==args.source,
+            'fresh replay requires checkout of exact qualified source')
+    require(not subprocess.check_output(['git','status','--porcelain','--','src','Cargo.toml','Cargo.lock'],cwd=repo,text=True).strip(),
+            'fresh Rust sources are dirty')
+    manifest=json.loads(args.inputs.read_bytes())
+    entries=manifest['inputs']
+    require(type(entries) is list and entries,'no exact inputs')
+    archive=zipfile.ZipFile(args.artifact) if args.artifact.is_file() else None
+    def read(member):
+        require(type(member) is str and not member.startswith('/') and '..' not in Path(member).parts,
+                'invalid artifact member')
+        if archive is not None:
+            require(len([i for i in archive.infolist() if i.filename==member])==1,'missing or duplicate input member')
+            return archive.read(member)
+        target=(args.artifact/member).resolve()
+        require(target.is_relative_to(args.artifact.resolve()),'input outside artifact')
+        return target.read_bytes()
+    try:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='independent-kernel-replay-') as private:
+            temp=Path(private)
+            seen=set()
+            for entry in entries:
+                identity=entry['sha256']
+                require(identity not in seen,'duplicate input identity')
+                seen.add(identity)
+                require(entry['expected_returncode'] in (0,1) and type(entry['expected_returncode']) is int,'invalid oracle expectation')
+                stored=read(entry['member'])
+                if 'compressed_member_sha256' in entry:
+                    require(sha(stored)==entry['compressed_member_sha256'],'compressed input identity mismatch')
+                    require(len(stored)==entry['compressed_member_bytes'],'compressed input size mismatch')
+                raw=gzip.decompress(stored) if entry['encoding']=='gzip' else stored
+                require(sha(raw)==identity and len(raw)==entry['bytes'],'exact input identity/size mismatch')
+                snapshot=temp/'current.ndjson'
+                snapshot.write_bytes(raw);snapshot.chmod(0o444)
+                config=temp/'config.json'
+                config.write_text(json.dumps(dict(export_file_path=str(snapshot),use_stdin=False,
+                    permitted_axioms=['propext','Classical.choice','Quot.sound'],unpermitted_axiom_hard_error=True,
+                    num_threads=1,nat_extension=True,string_extension=True,print_success_message=True)))
+                input_folder=args.out/identity;input_folder.mkdir()
+                (input_folder/'config.json').write_bytes(config.read_bytes())
+                observation=dict(input=entry,config_sha256=sha(config.read_bytes()),oracles={})
+                report['inputs'].append(observation)
+                for label,binary in binaries.items():
+                    command=[str(binary),str(config)] if label=='rust' else [str(binary),'--from-export',str(snapshot)]
+                    before=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN);tick=time.perf_counter()
+                    try:
+                        result=subprocess.run(command,capture_output=True,timeout=args.timeout)
+                        code,out,err,timed_out=result.returncode,result.stdout,result.stderr,False
+                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as failure:
+                        code,out,err,timed_out=None,failure.stdout or b'',failure.stderr or b'',True
+                    wall=time.perf_counter()-tick;after=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
+                    folder=args.out/identity/label;folder.mkdir(parents=True)
+                    (folder/'stdout').write_bytes(out);(folder/'stderr').write_bytes(err)
+                    observation['oracles'][label]=dict(command=command,returncode=code,timed_out=timed_out,
+                        verdict=classify(code,timed_out),wall_seconds=wall,
+                        completed_child_cpu_seconds=after.ru_utime+after.ru_stime-before.ru_utime-before.ru_stime,
+                        stdout_sha256=sha(out),stderr_sha256=sha(err),input_sha256=sha(snapshot.read_bytes()),
+                        input_bytes=snapshot.stat().st_size)
+                    save()
+                    require(code==entry['expected_returncode'] and not timed_out,'independent kernel verdict mismatch: '+label+' '+identity)
+                    require(sha(snapshot.read_bytes())==identity,'fresh input changed during checking')
+                snapshot.chmod(0o644)
+                print(json.dumps(dict(input_sha256=identity,expected=entry['expected_returncode'],kernels=3,passed=True)),flush=True)
+        require({k:sha(v.read_bytes()) for k,v in binaries.items()}==binary_hashes,'executed binary changed')
+        report.update(completed=True,passed=True,unique_inputs=len(entries),real_kernel_processes=3*len(entries),
+                      acceptance_rejection_agreement=True)
+        save()
+    except Exception as error:
+        report['failure']=repr(error);save();raise
+    finally:
+        if archive is not None:archive.close()
+
+
+if __name__=='__main__':main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent standard-library typed-index and selected-partition checks.
+
+This file imports no implementation under review. Declaration ``own`` hashes
+are witnessed by the actual complete native-index output; this reader recomputes
+SCC closure and declaration schedule hashes from those own hashes/dependencies.
+The flattened index omits inductive block boundaries, so its ``complex`` digest
+cannot be regenerated from this representation alone and remains an exact
+full-native witness. Neither these identities nor a partition are proof
+acceptance or historical HMAC authentication.
+"""
+import hashlib
+import json
+
+SIMPLE = frozenset(('axiom', 'def', 'opaque', 'thm'))
+KINDS = SIMPLE | frozenset(('quot', 'itype', 'ctor', 'rec'))
+BUILTINS = tuple(('Quot Quot.mk Quot.lift Quot.ind String String.ofList Nat Nat.zero '
+                 'Nat.succ Nat.add Nat.sub Nat.mul Nat.pow Nat.mod Nat.div Nat.div.go '
+                 'Nat.modCore.go Nat.beq Nat.ble Nat.gcd Nat.land Nat.lor Nat.xor '
+                 'Nat.shiftLeft Nat.shiftRight Bool.true Bool.false Char Char.ofNat '
+                 'List List.nil List.cons').split())
+_INDEX_KEYS = frozenset(('meta', 'declarations', 'count', 'builtins', 'complex', 'schedule'))
+_DECL_KEYS = frozenset(('key', 'name', 'kind', 'own', 'deps', 'index', 'closure'))
+_DECISION_KEYS = frozenset(('name', 'index', 'status', 'reason', 'dependency_witness', 'evidence_id'))
+_VALIDATED_INDEXES = {}
+
+
+def require(condition, message):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def canonical(value):
+    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'),
+                      ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value)).hexdigest()
+
+
+def hexid(value):
+    return (type(value) is str and len(value) == 64 and
+            all(c in '0123456789abcdef' for c in value))
+
+
+def strict_object(pairs):
+    obj = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        require(key not in obj, 'duplicate JSON field')
+        obj[key] = value
+    return obj
+
+
+def _json_tree(value):
+    """Reject Python aliases/non-JSON objects before canonical comparison."""
+    if value is None or type(value) in (str, int, bool):
+        return
+    if type(value) is float:
+        # canonical rejects nonfinite IEEE numbers.
+        canonical(value)
+        return
+    if type(value) is list:
+        for child in value:
+            _json_tree(child)
+        return
+    if type(value) is dict:
+        require(all(type(k) is str for k in value), 'JSON object key is not a string')
+        for child in value.values():
+            _json_tree(child)
+        return
+    raise ValueError('non-JSON value in typed index')
+
+
+def _components(adjacency):
+    """Iterative Tarjan decomposition, emitting dependency components first."""
+    numbering, low, active, on_active, groups = {}, {}, [], set(), []
+    clock = 0
+    for first in adjacency:
+        if first in numbering:
+            continue
+        numbering[first] = low[first] = clock
+        clock += 1
+        active.append(first)
+        on_active.add(first)
+        frames = [(first, iter(adjacency[first]), None)]
+        while frames:
+            node, edges, parent = frames[-1]
+            try:
+                child = next(edges)
+            except StopIteration:
+                frames.pop()
+                if parent is not None:
+                    low[parent] = min(low[parent], low[node])
+                if low[node] == numbering[node]:
+                    group = []
+                    while True:
+                        member = active.pop()
+                        on_active.remove(member)
+                        group.append(member)
+                        if member == node:
+                            break
+                    groups.append(group)
+                continue
+            if child not in numbering:
+                numbering[child] = low[child] = clock
+                clock += 1
+                active.append(child)
+                on_active.add(child)
+                frames.append((child, iter(adjacency[child]), node))
+            elif child in on_active:
+                low[node] = min(low[node], numbering[child])
+    return groups
+
+
+def validate_index(index):
+    """Reject malformed full indexes and independently rederive their SCC roots."""
+    require(type(index) is dict and set(index) == _INDEX_KEYS, 'incomplete full native index')
+    _json_tree(index)
+    identity = digest(index)
+    if identity in _VALIDATED_INDEXES:
+        return dict(_VALIDATED_INDEXES[identity])
+    require(type(index['count']) is int and index['count'] >= 0, 'invalid declaration count')
+    require(type(index['declarations']) is list and len(index['declarations']) == index['count'],
+            'declaration count differs from complete rows')
+    require(type(index['meta']) is dict and type(index['meta'].get('format')) is dict and
+            index['meta']['format'].get('version') == '3.1.0', 'invalid export metadata domain')
+    require(hexid(index['complex']) and hexid(index['schedule']), 'invalid global/schedule fingerprint')
+    by_key, names = {}, set()
+    for position, row in enumerate(index['declarations']):
+        require(type(row) is dict and set(row) == _DECL_KEYS, 'incomplete full declaration identity')
+        require(type(row['index']) is int and row['index'] == position,
+                'noninteger or out-of-order declaration index')
+        require(type(row['name']) is str and row['name'] and row['name'] not in names,
+                'missing/duplicate displayed declaration name')
+        require(type(row['kind']) is str and row['kind'] in KINDS, 'unsupported declaration kind')
+        require(all(hexid(row[k]) for k in ('key', 'own', 'closure')) and row['key'] not in by_key,
+                'invalid or duplicate declaration fingerprint')
+        require(type(row['deps']) is list and all(hexid(x) for x in row['deps']) and
+                row['deps'] == sorted(set(row['deps'])) and row['key'] not in row['deps'],
+                'dependencies are not canonical unique direct identities')
+        by_key[row['key']] = row
+        names.add(row['name'])
+    require(index['schedule'] == digest([r['key'] for r in index['declarations']]),
+            'declaration schedule fingerprint differs from rows')
+    graph = {key: [dep for dep in row['deps'] if dep in by_key] for key, row in by_key.items()}
+    groups = _components(graph)
+    group_for = {key: n for n, group in enumerate(groups) for key in group}
+    roots = {}
+    for number, group in enumerate(groups):
+        outgoing = {group_for[dep] for key in group for dep in graph[key]
+                    if group_for[dep] != number}
+        require(all(other in roots for other in outgoing), 'SCC dependency order failed')
+        unresolved = {dep for key in group for dep in by_key[key]['deps'] if dep not in by_key}
+        roots[number] = digest(['scc', sorted([[key, by_key[key]['own']] for key in group]),
+                                sorted(roots[other] for other in outgoing), sorted(unresolved)])
+        require(all(by_key[key]['closure'] == roots[number] for key in group),
+                'SCC closure fingerprint differs from actual own/dependency rows')
+    builtins = index['builtins']
+    require(type(builtins) is dict and set(builtins) == set(BUILTINS),
+            'incomplete or unexpected builtin identity universe')
+    by_name = {r['name']: r for r in index['declarations']}
+    for name, pair in builtins.items():
+        require(type(pair) is list and len(pair) == 2 and
+                all(part is None or hexid(part) for part in pair), 'invalid builtin fingerprint pair')
+        key, root = pair
+        if key is None:
+            require(root is None and name not in by_name, 'missing declared builtin identity')
+        elif key in by_key:
+            require(by_key[key]['name'] == name and root == by_key[key]['closure'],
+                    'builtin closure/name differs from full declaration')
+        else:
+            require(root is None and name not in by_name, 'unresolved builtin carries a false closure')
+    proof = dict(index_sha256=identity, declarations=index['count'], strongly_connected_components=len(groups),
+                 independently_recomputed_closures=True, independently_recomputed_schedule=True,
+                 own_and_complex_scope='actual full-native index witnesses; not independently reconstructed from export DAG')
+    if len(_VALIDATED_INDEXES) >= 256:
+        _VALIDATED_INDEXES.clear()
+    _VALIDATED_INDEXES[identity] = proof
+    return dict(proof)
+
+
+def independent_partition(parent_index, current_index, *, compatible=True):
+    """Return the authorized prefix/dependency rule and its exact reasons."""
+    validate_index(parent_index)
+    validate_index(current_index)
+    same_metadata = canonical(parent_index['meta']) == canonical(current_index['meta'])
+    compatible = bool(compatible and same_metadata)
+    globals_same = bool(compatible and
+        canonical(parent_index['builtins']) == canonical(current_index['builtins']) and
+        parent_index['complex'] == current_index['complex'])
+    schedule_same = bool(globals_same and parent_index['schedule'] == current_index['schedule'])
+    previous = {r['key']: r for r in parent_index['declarations']} if compatible else {}
+    prefix, checked, reused, reasons = True, [], [], []
+    for row in current_index['declarations']:
+        prior = previous.get(row['key'])
+        prefix = bool(prefix and globals_same and prior is not None and
+                      prior['index'] == row['index'] and prior['own'] == row['own'])
+        local = bool(schedule_same and row['kind'] in SIMPLE and prior is not None and
+                     prior['own'] == row['own'] and prior['closure'] == row['closure'])
+        reuse = prefix or local
+        (reused if reuse else checked).append(row['index'])
+        if reuse:
+            reason = 'exact_verified_prefix' if prefix else 'dependency_closure_unchanged'
+        elif not compatible:
+            reason = 'toolchain_or_policy_changed'
+        elif not globals_same:
+            reason = 'global_builtin_or_complex_assumption_changed'
+        elif not schedule_same:
+            reason = 'declaration_schedule_changed'
+        elif row['kind'] not in SIMPLE:
+            reason = 'complex_outside_verified_prefix'
+        else:
+            reason = 'content_or_transitive_dependency_changed'
+        reasons.append(reason)
+    return checked, reused, reasons
+
+
+def validate_partition(result, parent_index, current_index, parent_evidence, *, parent_provenance=None):
+    """Validate every accepted decision, evidence origin, and actual selected count.
+
+    A caller that supplies only indexes must independently bind unchanged
+    verifier provenance in its receipt-chain review. Supplying parent_provenance
+    additionally enforces that binding here.
+    """
+    require(type(result) is dict and result.get('schema') == 'mathgraph.incremental-lean.v1' and
+            result.get('status') == 'VERIFIED' and result.get('action_authorization') == 'NONE',
+            'result is not bounded verified evidence')
+    require(hexid(parent_evidence) and result.get('previous_evidence') == parent_evidence and
+            hexid(result.get('evidence_id')), 'result evidence parent is missing or substituted')
+    require(type(result.get('provenance')) is dict, 'missing verifier provenance')
+    compatible = parent_provenance is None or canonical(result['provenance']) == canonical(parent_provenance)
+    require(compatible, 'verifier provenance changed across accepted predecessor chain')
+    checked, reused, reasons = independent_partition(parent_index, current_index, compatible=compatible)
+    decisions = result.get('decisions')
+    require(type(decisions) is list and len(decisions) == current_index['count'],
+            'complete per-declaration decisions missing')
+    selected = set(checked)
+    for position, (decision, row, reason) in enumerate(zip(decisions, current_index['declarations'], reasons)):
+        require(type(decision) is dict and set(decision) == _DECISION_KEYS,
+                'incomplete or unexpected decision fields')
+        require(type(decision['index']) is int and decision['index'] == position and
+                decision['name'] == row['name'], 'decision declaration identity/order differs')
+        expected_status = 'VERIFIED_NEW' if position in selected else 'VERIFIED_REUSED'
+        expected_evidence = result['evidence_id'] if position in selected else parent_evidence
+        require(decision['status'] == expected_status and decision['reason'] == reason and
+                decision['evidence_id'] == expected_evidence,
+                'decision status/reason/evidence origin differs from independent rule')
+        witness = dict(own=row['own'], closure=row['closure'], direct=row['deps'])
+        require(canonical(decision['dependency_witness']) == canonical(witness),
+                'decision witness differs from complete native index')
+    expected_counts = dict(total=current_index['count'], rechecked=len(checked), scheduled=len(checked),
+                           invalidated=len(checked), reused=len(reused))
+    counts = result.get('counts')
+    require(type(counts) is dict and set(counts) == set(expected_counts) and
+            all(type(counts[name]) is int and counts[name] == value for name, value in expected_counts.items()),

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Targeted real-fixture reader falsifiers; no input copying or source mutation."""
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from reviewer import Reviewer, validate_structure
+
+
+def run(artifact,repo,source,output):
+    observed=[]
+    def refuse(label,action):
+        try:action()
+        except (ValueError,KeyError,FileNotFoundError) as error:
+            observed.append(dict(case=label,status='REFUSED',reason=type(error).__name__+': '+str(error)))
+        else:raise AssertionError('falsifier accepted: '+label)
+    base=Reviewer(artifact,repo,source,True)
+    fake=copy.deepcopy(base.report);fake.update(repetitions=0,cycles=0,profiles={},requested_profiles=[])
+    refuse('fake-passed-zero-work',lambda:validate_structure(fake,True))
+    missing=Reviewer(artifact,repo,source,True)
+    first=next(iter(missing.report['profiles'].values()))['pairs'][0]['steps'][0]
+    member=missing.store.join(missing.store.lifecycle,first['export_witness']['artifact_relative_path'])
+    del missing.store.members[member]
+    refuse('missing-complete-input-object',missing.run)
+    corrupt=Reviewer(artifact,repo,source,True)
+    first=next(iter(corrupt.report['profiles'].values()))['pairs'][0]['steps'][0]
+    first['export_witness']['sha256']='0'*64
+    refuse('changed-compressed-input-digest',corrupt.run)
+    parent=Reviewer(artifact,repo,source,True)
+    first=next(iter(parent.report['profiles'].values()))['pairs'][0]['steps'][0]
+    target=first['result_witness']['uncompressed_sha256'];original=parent.store.archive_json
+    def changed(record):
+        value=original(record)
+        if record['uncompressed_sha256']==target:
+            value['previous_evidence']='0'*64
+        return value
+    parent.store.archive_json=changed
+    refuse('raw-result-parent-substitution',parent.run)
+    coverage=Reviewer(artifact,repo,source,True)
+    for profile in coverage.report['profiles'].values():
+        for pair in profile['pairs']:
+            for step in pair['steps']:step['export_witness']=None
+    refuse('all-changed-input-descriptors-omitted',coverage.run)
+    result=dict(status='PASS_DIRECTED_FAIL_CLOSED_FALSIFIERS',qualified=False,
+                mutation_scope='Temporary in-memory artifact views; no source or full-input file was changed/copied.',
+                cases=observed)
+    Path(output).write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
+    print(json.dumps(result))
+
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    p.add_argument('--artifact',type=Path,required=True);p.add_argument('--repo',type=Path,required=True)
+    p.add_argument('--source',required=True);p.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True)
+    a=p.parse_args();run(a.artifact,a.repo,a.source,a.output)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Scoped decoded control-report cap: large valid gzip JSON, no full extraction."""
+import contextlib
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import unittest
+
+import controls
+
+ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+BIG=ROOT/'controls-cap-fixture-65mib.json.gz'
+SMALL=ROOT/'controls-cap-fixture-small.json.gz'
+ACTUAL_CHAIN=ROOT/'chain-wrapper-cap-fixture-actual-expanded.json.gz'
+PAYLOAD=65*1024*1024
+
+
+def hashes(path):
+ def one(encoded):
+  h=hashlib.sha256();length=0
+  with path.open('rb') as raw:
+   with (gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=raw) if encoded else contextlib.nullcontext(raw)) as source:
+    for chunk in iter(lambda:source.read(1<<20),b''):
+     h.update(chunk);length+=len(chunk)
+  return h.hexdigest(),length
+ return one(False),one(True)
+
+
+class Store:
+ artifact=''
+ def __init__(self,large_tests=False,oversized=False):
+  self.paths={}
+  self.records=[]
+  for folder in ('revision-chain-tests-original','revision-chain-tests-expanded',
+                 'revision-chain-controls-original','revision-chain-controls-expanded'):
+   member=folder+'/summary.json.gz'
+   path=(BIG if 'controls' in folder else ACTUAL_CHAIN if large_tests and folder=='revision-chain-tests-expanded' else SMALL)
+   self.paths[member]=path
+   compressed,decoded=hashes(path)
+   self.records.append(dict(path=member,sha256=compressed[0],bytes=compressed[1],
+                           uncompressed_path=member[:-3],uncompressed_sha256=decoded[0],
+                           uncompressed_bytes=(512*1024*1024+1 if (oversized is True and 'controls-original' in folder) or (oversized=='chain' and 'tests-expanded' in folder) else decoded[1])))
+  self.members=set(self.paths)|{'revision-control-archive.json'}
+ def join(self,*parts):return '/'.join(str(x).strip('/') for x in parts if str(x).strip('/'))
+ def map(self,path):return path
+ def json(self,path):
+  assert path=='revision-control-archive.json'
+  return self.records
+ def stream_hash(self,member,gzip_encoded=False):return hashes(self.paths[member])[1 if gzip_encoded else 0]
+ @contextlib.contextmanager
+ def open(self,member):
+  with self.paths[member].open('rb') as f:yield f
+
+
+class ControlCapTests(unittest.TestCase):
+ @classmethod
+ def setUpClass(cls):
+  if not BIG.exists():
+   with BIG.open('wb') as raw,gzip.GzipFile(filename='',fileobj=raw,mode='wb',mtime=0) as f:
+    f.write(b'{"payload":"')
+    for _ in range(65):f.write(b'x'*(1024*1024))
+    f.write(b'"}')
+  if not SMALL.exists():
+   with SMALL.open('wb') as raw,gzip.GzipFile(filename='',fileobj=raw,mode='wb',mtime=0) as f:f.write(b'{}')
+ def test_control_report_decodes_valid_json_above_generic64mib(self):
+  store=Store()
+  value=controls._report(store,'revision-chain-controls-original/summary.json.gz')
+  self.assertEqual(len(value['payload']),PAYLOAD)
+ def test_manifest_accepts_large_control_reports(self):
+  observed=controls._manifest(Store())
+  self.assertEqual(len(observed),4)
+ def test_actual_expanded_chain_wrapper_above64mib_is_valid(self):
+  self.assertGreater(hashes(ACTUAL_CHAIN)[1][1],64*1024*1024)
+  self.assertEqual(len(controls._manifest(Store(large_tests=True))),4)
+ def test_chain_descriptor_above512mib_refuses(self):
+  with self.assertRaises(ValueError):controls._manifest(Store(oversized='chain'))
+ def test_control_descriptor_above512mib_refuses(self):
+  with self.assertRaises(ValueError):controls._manifest(Store(oversized=True))
+

+        selected.append(3)
+    rows=[]
+    for row in current['declarations']:
+        checked=row['index'] in selected
+        rows.append(dict(name=row['name'], index=row['index'],
+                         status='VERIFIED_NEW' if checked else 'VERIFIED_REUSED',
+                         reason=('complex_outside_verified_prefix' if row['kind']=='quot' else

+                                ('exact_verified_prefix' if not selected else 'dependency_closure_unchanged'),
+                         evidence_id='b'*64 if checked else parent,
+                         dependency_witness=dict(own=row['own'],closure=row['closure'],direct=row['deps'])))

+
